issues.title: Agentic framework design  & replay buffer
issues.body:
Hi Roll developers,

I'm currently trying to integrate some new tool usages into the agentic environment, but I found the code in `roll/pipeline/agentic/environment_worker.py` a bit hard to follow.

It seems that this file contains a lot of prompt-related logic, including prompt inspection and reformatting. In my opinion, the responsibility of `EnvironmentWorker` should be kept minimal and more focused on coordination rather than handling prompt-specific tasks. These kinds of tasks could be better encapsulated within each individual environment implementation. Otherwise, we might end up adding many if-else branches to support different environments, which reduces modularity and makes it harder to extend with diverse environments.

Moreover, I think it would be helpful to consider introducing a replay buffer mechanism, similar to what's used in classic RL settings (e.g., using the most recent 4 frames as observation) or as implemented in Verl-agent. This can help decouple agent learning from full trajectory dependencies and improve training efficiency.

Thanks for your great work on this project! Looking forward to your thoughts.

issues.title: AssertionError in list_of_dict_to_dict_of_list during validation in AgenticPipeline
issues.body:
When running start_agentic_pipeline.py, the pipeline crashes during validation with an AssertionError inside list_of_dict_to_dict_of_list. It seems that the rollout batches from different workers return dictionaries with inconsistent keys, causing the concatenation to fail.

Run cmd:
```
bash examples/qwen2.5-0.5B-agentic/run_agentic_pipeline_sokoban.sh
```

Error Trace:
```
ray.exceptions.RayTaskError(AssertionError): ray::RolloutScheduler.get_batch()
  File "roll/distributed/scheduler/protocol.py", line 96, in list_of_dict_to_dict_of_list
    assert key in output
AssertionError
```

linked_prs.title: (Fix)  DataProto.concat would raise an error when workers returned meta_info["metrics"] with inconsistent keys

ai_judgment.response: Yes. The issue involves a failure in the execution of an agent's workflow (AgenticPipeline), specifically during validation, which aligns with the "Workflow issues" category in the agent issue taxonomy. The error occurs in the orchestration of rollout batches, leading to a crash, indicating a workflow anomaly.
